inputs.text: The turmoil involving the US, Israel and Iran exposes how ordinary Indian families are left vulnerable by dependence on imported crude and decisions made far beyond their control. Stable petrol and diesel prices and excise-duty cuts may offer relief, but it’s unfair to treat support for households as the problem while leaving the underlying dependence untouched. Energy security must mean more than sovereignty: it should mean a planned transition that protects workers and low-income families, and doesn’t make them pay the price of shocks or reform.
